reviewBoundary: Three complete junior fifteen-gap originals. Fictional parcel, supervised kite and photograph-exhibition cases. Same-author all-alternative/context review, no independent calibration.

materials.title: A parcel for Sam
materials.text:
A parcel with my brother Sam’s name arrived a month before his birthday. We were ____1____. The box was long and light.

Mum checked the address. The street was right, but the house number was ____2____. Another Sam lived three doors away. My brother sighed.

We took it to Sam, an older model-ship repairer. He thanked us and said he had been waiting for a new ____3____. He opened the box and showed us a thin wooden mast, carefully wrapped.

My brother's disappointment changed to ____4____. He made paper boats, but had never seen so many tiny ropes. We looked together while Mum stayed.

One rope was hanging loose. The man pointed to it and asked what we thought it did. My brother guessed it was ____5____. Sam showed how it supported part of the mast. Something that looked like decoration had a practical ____6____.

 Before leaving, my brother asked whether he could return with his paper boat. Sam suggested the next afternoon. We wrote it down rather than assuming that an open door meant he was always ____7____.

On Sunday, the two Sams compared their boats. The paper one had no little ropes, but its folded shape made it surprisingly ____8____. The wooden model needed a different ____9____.

My brother brought home new ideas. He had not received a birthday ____10____. He had found someone nearby who enjoyed thinking about ships. Later, the post worker apologised for the wrong number. Sam reported no ____11____, but Mum requested better address checks. A happy result did not make wrong delivery a good ____12____. He added to his notes: ask what a small part ____13____ before deciding it is unnecessary. Then he checked the calendar. His actual birthday was still weeks ____14____. For once, he did not ____15____ waiting.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: An unexpected non-birthday parcel puzzles the family. Sleep/hunger/lateness do not explain curiosity.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The wrong house number explains another Sam three doors away. Missing/colour/size do not describe the mistaken numerical address.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: A mast is a model-ship part. Ticket/cake/letter do not name the thin wooden component.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Interest in the detailed model replaces disappointment. Anger/fear/sleep do not match asking and looking.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: He guesses decoration before learning support function. Broken/invisible/edible do not contrast decorative with practical.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Supporting the mast is the rope’s purpose. Price/owner/colour do not name its function.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: A visit needs a time when Sam is available. Correct/famous/finished do not indicate free time to receive them.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Folds can make the paper structure strong. Cost/wetness/speed do not name structural resistance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Different models need appropriate standards. Address/calendar/scissors do not define assessment criteria.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: A birthday present is the gift he first imagined. Number/rope/promise are not that expected parcel role.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The wrong delivery caused no harm. Interest/friendship/conversation occurred, so no before those would be false.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Wrong delivery is not good practice even after a happy result. Birthday/model/picture do not name a repeated delivery procedure.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: He checks what a part does, its function. Cost/weight/appearance alone do not identify the supporting role.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: A future birthday is weeks away. Ago is past and inside/below spatial.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: He does not mind waiting because of his new interest. Finish/start/forget do not express acceptance of the wait.

materials.title: The mark on the kite line
materials.text:
At a supervised kite afternoon, we took turns with one kite. The instructor explained handling and the marked area. I watched the kite's colours, hardly noticing the ____1____.

I wanted it higher immediately. The instructor asked me to look at a small mark on the line. It showed the agreed ____2____ for that session. More line did not suit the space.

Changed wind made it dip. I pulled hard in surprise, but the instructor guided me through a steadier response. I had been treating every movement as a sign of ____3____ rather than first noticing what had changed.

Tessa watched safely beside us. I looked at my hands whenever uncertain. "You miss the kite when you do that," she said. Next time, I kept my attention ____4____ between the line and the sky.

We stopped when the instructor judged conditions unsuitable. But I understood more of what I was ____5____. 

We drew the kite. Mine had a red tail. Tessa added a tiny hand and a line below hers. I had drawn the visible ____6____ and left out the connection that made it a shared task.

The instructor gathered and checked the equipment. We helped only with the jobs we had been ____7____. 

My sister asked if I had flown highest. I showed her the notebook instead of claiming a ____8____. The afternoon had not been a contest. I could explain the line's mark, the changes in wind and why we had ____9____ when we did. Those details helped explain the ____10____. My sister drew her own picture. This time, the line was not ____11____. It led down to a small group, all looking up. I liked her drawing because it included the ____12____ around the bright shape. Without that, the kite might have looked completely ____13____. It was not. The flight depended on people, equipment and ____14____. A picture could show the colours; telling the story helped show how they stayed in the ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: He attends to colours but not the line, central next. Weather/people are not the newly marked equipment connection; colours repeats what he noticed.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The mark gives the agreed line limit. Price/winner/date do not constrain height in available space.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: He overreacts by treating movement as failure. Sunlight/permission/decoration do not name his anxious negative judgment.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: He moves attention between hand/line and sky. Fixed/lost/hidden do not describe active switching.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: He understands the activity he is doing. Buying/drawing/winning do not name the current guided flight.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The coloured kite is the visible object, while guidance/limits are less visible relations. Other nouns do not name what he drew.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: They assist with jobs shown/taught to them. Selling/forgetting/refusing does not establish appropriate handling.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: A height comparison invites a victory claim, which he rejects. Picture/lesson/line are not winning.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: He explains stopping when conditions required it. Laughter/painting and starting alone do not describe the instructor’s limit decision.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Conditions and limits explain the experience. Colour/sister/notebook alone do not name the whole activity.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The sister includes the line rather than omitting it. Length/visibility/straightness do not express the correction to his first drawing.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The picture includes people/line around the kite, an arrangement. Cost/race/error are not that context.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Without connections the kite might look independent. Brightness/distance/colour are visible properties still possible with connections.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Wind and safe circumstances are conditions affecting flight. Prizes/sales/paint alone do not complete the support system.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Kite colours stay aloft in the air. Box/river/classroom are not the described flying place.

materials.title: The photograph with two stories
materials.text:
Maya found an old swimming-pool photograph in her father’s album for an exhibition. A boy stood beside the empty pool holding a bucket. She wrote a ____1____ saying he was helping clean it.

Her father disagreed. The boy was his younger brother, and the bucket held model boats. The closed pool’s supervised area had hosted a model-boat club ____2____. A temporary tank nearby was being filled.

The bucket’s contents were invisible. She had turned an uncertain object into a confident ____3____. The image alone did not establish cleaning.

Her father was unsure of the year. A nearby album page held a dated notice. It gave stronger support for the date than the boy's ____4____, which could have suited several summers.

Maya added the event and notice’s date. She also identified her father as the source of the boy's name and purpose. The picture and the recollection were ____5____ evidence, not the same thing.

A visitor recalled lessons at the pool. Maya invited a written memory. The new account could ____6____ the history without changing who the photographed boy was.

Another visitor guessed cleaning. Maya understood the guess; she had made it herself. She could explain why it was a ____7____ reading rather than an established fact.

The exhibition did not lose its interest when the captions became more careful. People asked ____8____ questions because they could see what was known and what still depended on memory. A notice explained how new information could be offered and ____9____.

Maya kept her first caption as an early ____10____. It showed how an action could be invented. She did not decide that photographs were ____11____. She decided that their strength grew when their limits were understood. The bucket remained the same bucket; what changed was the ____12____ placed around it. Looking closely meant noticing both visible details and the questions they could not ____13____. The next picture had no people. She wrote down the location, then paused before adding a ____14____. There might be more than one plausible story, and plausibility was not yet ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: A caption describes a photograph. Ticket/price/song do not name the exhibit text.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The supervised model-boat club event is described. Accident/sale/cleaning lesson contradict the context.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: She inferred cleaning, an action. Colour/date/name are not that assumed activity.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Clothes can fit several summers and weakly date the image. Contents are not visible, address/voice not the pictured dating clue.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Image and recollection are different kinds of evidence. Identical is explicitly denied; neither uselessness nor secrecy follows.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: A lesson memory adds/enriches history. Erasing/replacing would remove earlier material and permanent completion is not promised.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: A cleaning scene is a possible reading of visible cues, but the fuller evidence does not establish it. Proven/correct assert truth and complete ignores the missing context.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Knowing evidence and uncertainty lets visitors ask more precise questions. Less relevant/purely personal/completely unanswerable do not follow from the clarified context.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: New information can be checked before adoption. Guarantee/ignore/purchase do not describe assessment.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The first caption is an early draft, not settled fact. It is neither instruction nor authorization.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: She avoids declaring images useless. They remain detailed/interesting/historical, so those are not the negative absolute rejected.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The explanatory account around the bucket changes. Water/paint/clothing do not name the narrative interpretation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Some questions cannot be answered by visible details alone. Raising/hiding/repeating do not mean resolving them.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: She already records location then pauses before adding a narrative. The other objects are not the story she is cautious about inventing.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Plausibility is not proof. It already involves possibility/imagination and can be interesting, so those are not the evidential threshold.
